rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis uses uniaxial tensile loading on a bulk FeNiCrMn HEA, while the target uses nanoindentation/friction on a FeNiCrCoCu coating on a Cu substrate. These are different kinds of interventions (tensile vs. indentation/friction).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis uses vacuum, Nose-Hoover thermostat, and temperatures of 10, 300, 600 K, while the target uses periodic/contractive boundaries, Langevin thermostat, and temperatures of 300, 600, 900, 1200 K. The temperature ranges overlap only at 300 and 600 K, and the boundary conditions and thermostat differ.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis focuses on dislocation nucleation at vacancy clusters and Shockley partials forming stacking faults, while the target focuses on lattice disorder, dislocation density reduction, and a shift from stacking faults to lattice disorder at high temperature. Both involve dislocation-mediated plasticity, but the specific pathways and structural mediators differ.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts yield strength trends with temperature and strain rate, while the target predicts hardness, elastic modulus, and friction coefficient trends with temperature. The properties measured are different (yield strength vs. hardness/friction).
